fail_rules: If the image reads as abstract, atmosphere-first, texture-only, or subjectless, it must FAIL.
If the image does not read as a manufactured object immediately, it must FAIL.
If the ceramic read turns glossy, plastic, PVC-like, or toy-like, it must FAIL.
Check histogram skew: shadows should dominate and highlights must stay diffuse.
Check saturation: reject neon, RGB-clean, or oversaturated reads.
Check color harmony: reject pure white, pure black, and synthetic magenta drift.
Check material-color match: color must feel materially bonded, never flat digital fill.
material_read: Abstract digital pattern with neon and oversaturated colors, resembling a digital filter or noise rather than a physical material.
fix_direction: Re-establish a clear, singular manufactured object as the primary subject.
Drastically reduce saturation and shift the palette towards low saturation, shadow-heavy tones.
Eliminate all neon, RGB-clean, and synthetic colors; aim for a porcelain-white base with subtle subtractive mineral color logic.
Develop a matte, dry, dense ceramic material read with ultra-controlled eggshell microtexture.
Ensure colors are materially bonded to the surface, avoiding any flat digital fill appearance.
Introduce clear contour evidence (edge, rim, bevel, seam, curvature) to define the object.
summary: The image fails completely as a white ceramic material study. It is an abstract, highly saturated digital pattern with prominent neon green, blue, and pink colors, bearing no resemblance to a manufactured object or matte ceramic. The material read is closer to glossy plastic or digital noise, violating multiple core requirements for color, saturation, object readability, and material properties.
